finding: Against the httptest fake BOTH clients passed all seven capabilities. Against a real engine the Python client's parallel_tool_calls request fails: llama.cpp returns 'Failed to parse input at pos 47' on this model's tool schema, reproduced by calling the engine directly with the same body. The fake accepted a request a real backend rejects.
attribution: This is llama.cpp's limitation with the Llama-3.2 chat template, not a merc defect. It counts anyway: merc advertises OpenAI tool-call compatibility, and a buyer whose code sends tools gets a 500 from whichever backend is serving them. The capability is backend-dependent and merc does not currently say so.
why_it_matters: This is the argument for real-runtime proof stated as a measurement rather than a principle. Every conformance number merc had before today was taken against a server that agreed with whatever it was sent.
lane_status_reason: Not promoted to CANARY_PROVEN. Six of seven capabilities is not conformance, and the honest status for a lane that fails against the only real backend available is not 'proven'.
